system.name: Acto
system.one_liner: the first automatic end-to-end testing technique for cloud system operators, using a state-centric testing approach

components.name: kubectl
components.role: user-facing client used to submit the upscale request

components.name: ZooKeeper CR
components.role: custom resource declaring the desired ZooKeeper state, edited to change replicas from 2 to 3

components.name: ZooKeeper Operator
components.role: operator that reconciles the managed ZooKeeper cluster toward the declared CR state

components.name: Kubernetes Core
components.role: Kubernetes control-plane components that maintain state objects and their controllers

components.name: State Objects
components.role: etcd-backed state objects (Pod, Vol) representing current cluster entities

components.name: Pod
components.role: state object representing a ZooKeeper replica pod

components.name: Vol
components.role: state object representing a ZooKeeper replica's storage volume

components.name: Statefulset Controller
components.role: Kubernetes controller that increases the stateful-set replica count and creates new pods

components.name: Volume Controller
components.role: Kubernetes controller that creates new persistent volumes for new replicas

components.name: Managed ZooKeeper
components.role: the actual running ZooKeeper cluster whose Pods and Vols are updated to match the desired state

components.name: Pods
components.role: resulting ZooKeeper pods after scale-up (three shown)

components.name: Vols
components.role: resulting ZooKeeper volumes after scale-up (three shown)

flows.what: reconciliation request to increase stateful-set count

content.key_idea: A single CR edit (bumping ZooKeeper replicas from 2 to 3) flows through the ZooKeeper Operator and Kubernetes' built-in state-object controllers to produce a new Pod and Volume in the managed cluster.
content.reading_order: Left to right: kubectl issues the edited CR, into the ZooKeeper Operator, through Kubernetes Core's state-object controllers, ending at the managed ZooKeeper Pods/Vols on the right.

red highlight on the changed replica value (3 <- 2) in the CR

style.stroke: dashed border around the Kubernetes Core boundary, solid on other boxes
style.font: mixed serif (Times) labels with Consolas monospace for the CR YAML snippet, 6-10.5pt
style.arrows: straight arrows with solid triangular heads
style.icons: bitmap/vector icons depicting a kubectl user, pods (cubes), and volumes (cylinders)

encoding.color_means: peach = ZooKeeper Operator, light blue = Kubernetes Core control-plane box, red = the changed replica value (2 to 3) in the CR, dark blue = arrows/box headers
encoding.line_style_means: dashed border delineates the Kubernetes Core boundary from the operator and the managed system
encoding.emphasis: the red-highlighted diff (3 <- 2) in the CR draws the eye to exactly what changed, tracing the causal chain from that one edit to new Pods/Vols on the right
reusable_patterns: single concrete before/after example (2 to 3 replicas) tracing a declarative config change through a control loop to concrete resources
weaknesses: ellipsis boxes elide most of the reconciliation loop, showing only the pod/volume path

evidence: Figure 3 shows how a ZooKeeper operator scales up a managed ZooKeeper cluster.
the operator notifies Kubernetes to increase the stateful-set count for replicas
Kubernetes creates a new pod and a new volume

summary: This figure illustrates, as background motivation for Acto, how a Kubernetes ZooKeeper operator scales a managed cluster from 2 to 3 replicas. A user issues kubectl to submit an edited custom resource (CR) that changes the replicas field from 2 to 3 (highlighted in red). The ZooKeeper Operator picks up this desired-state declaration and asks Kubernetes Core, whose Statefulset and Volume controllers read the current Pod/Vol state objects (backed by etcd) and create a new pod and a new volume. The result, a Managed ZooKeeper cluster with three pods and three volumes, appears on the right. Drawn as a left-to-right flow with peach, light-blue, and light-yellow flat-filled boxes, dark-blue arrows, and small pod/volume icons, the figure motivates Acto's state-centric testing approach by showing the operator's reconcile loop from declaration to concrete cluster state.
summary_zh: 该图以 ZooKeeper 为例，展示 Kubernetes 运算符如何将副本数从 2 扩容到 3：用户通过 kubectl 提交修改后的 CR，运算符驱动 Kubernetes 核心的 StatefulSet 与 Volume 控制器创建新 Pod 和卷。
